excerpt: Taskcue: a visual canvas for the coding agents already on your computer. Claude Code and Codex sessions side by side, on one board. - taskcue/taskcue
content_html:
A visual canvas for the coding agents already on your computer. Claude Code and Codex sessions side by side on one board, grouped by project. See what each one is doing, answer what it asks, and talk to any of them from one place.

Taskcue doesn't have its own model and doesn't sell AI usage. It drives the agents you have installed: the real claude and codex programs, with your own sign-in, settings, memory files, skills and MCP servers. A session started here is the same session you'd get in a terminal, and you can continue it there.

What it does

  • What needs you, on one page. When a session finishes a turn, Taskcue reads its reply once with your own agent and decides whether it needs you. If it does, you get a card: the question in a line, the options with the recommended one marked, and whether it's your call, needs your hands (a sign-in, a code), or is something the agent could have done itself. One press answers it. Open the session right under its card to talk it through.
  • One board for every agent. Each project folder is a frame; each session is a card with its agent, its state (working, needs you, ready, stopped) and what it was asked.
  • Claude Code and Codex, side by side. Start either in any project, pick its model, and choose how much it may do without asking.
  • Approvals in one place. When an agent wants to run a command or edit a file, the card turns amber and the panel shows exactly what it wants to do: Allow, Allow for this session, or Deny.
  • Your existing sessions too. Recent conversations from Claude Code's and Codex's own history appear on the board. Open one to read it; send a message to continue it.
  • Local only. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 and checks a secret token on every call, so other websites and programs on your computer can't drive your agents.

What needs you

The page Taskcue opens on. At the top, every session Taskcue runs that is waiting on you, across agents and projects: agents asking before they act, and cards for turns that ended on something for you. Below them, what is working and what is ready, each with its last reply in a line.

A card holds what the reply asks, in plain words:

  • Its options, each with what the reply says it costs and gets you, and the one it recommends marked. Picked options turn green; a question you could want several answers to takes several picks.
  • One main button, named for what it sends: Send “MIT”, Send 2 answers, Send “Done” for a step you did, Send it back when the agent could have done it itself. Hover it to read the exact message. With nothing picked it sends the recommended answer; with only your own words typed, it sends your words.
  • Decline tells the session no and is final: that ask doesn't come back from that session, however it's worded.
  • The X takes a card off with nothing sent, and is final too.
  • The files the turn wrote, one press away.

When you write to a session yourself, its card steps aside until the session replies; the reading of that reply takes its place. A card you decided never comes back.

What it costs. Each finished turn is read once, by one short call on the agent you already use, with no tools and nothing saved to its history: Sonnet on Claude Code (about 3 seconds), or Codex's own model at low effort. It runs on your own sign-in and counts toward your plan like any other use. TASKCUE_READER=0 turns it off.

Tuning it. pnpm replay reads your own recent Claude Code turns the same way and writes a report of the cards it would have made to ~/.taskcue/replay/ (never commit it: it holds your conversations). To try other instructions, put them in ~/.taskcue/reader.md. More in docs/needs-you.md.

Requirements

  • Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm
  • At least one agent, installed and signed in:
    • Claude Code: install it, then run claude once to sign in.
    • Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex, then codex login. (On macOS, the copy inside the ChatGPT desktop app is found too.)
  • macOS or Linux. Windows is untested.

Quick start

git clone https://github.com/taskcue/taskcue.git
cd taskcue
pnpm install
pnpm dev

Open the address it prints; it ends in #token=…. That's it.

For a production build: pnpm build && pnpm start.

Settings

Variable Default What it does
TASKCUE_PORT 4880 The port the server listens on (always 127.0.0.1).
TASKCUE_DATA_DIR ~/.taskcue Taskcue's own state: settings, the session list, the cards, the token.
TASKCUE_HISTORY on 0 keeps sessions from the agents' own history off the board.
TASKCUE_CLAUDE_BIN found on PATH The claude binary to use.
TASKCUE_CODEX_BIN found on PATH The codex binary to use.
TASKCUE_READER the session's own agent Which agent reads finished turns: claude, codex, or 0 for none (no cards).
TASKCUE_READER_MODEL Sonnet; Codex's default The model the reader asks for, by its agent's name for it. Set it with TASKCUE_READER.

Permissions

Each session starts in one of three modes, mapped onto each agent's own settings:

Mode Claude Code Codex
Ask first (default) default permission mode untrusted approvals, workspace-write sandbox
Edit freely acceptEdits on-request approvals, workspace-write sandbox
Full access bypassPermissions no approvals, no sandbox

Full access means the agent can run anything without asking. Use it only in a folder you'd trust it with.

How it works

browser (React, React Flow)  ──HTTP + SSE──▶  server (Node, no framework)
                                                │
                                                ├─ adapters/claude ──stdio, stream-json──▶  claude -p …
                                                └─ adapters/codex  ──stdio, JSON-RPC────▶  codex app-server

Each agent sits behind one small interface (server/agents/types.ts): start or resume a session, send a message, interrupt, answer an approval, read history. An adapter translates its agent's own events into Taskcue's (messages, tool calls, approvals) and the rest of the app never sees an agent's wire format. Conversations stay where each agent keeps them (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions); Taskcue only remembers which sessions are on the board.

More in docs/architecture.md. Adding another agent (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, anything that speaks the Agent Client Protocol) is one adapter: docs/adding-an-agent.md.

Your accounts

Taskcue runs each agent's own, unmodified program, and you sign in to it the agent's own way. Taskcue never reads, stores or forwards your credentials, and your usage is billed to your own account under your agreement with that provider. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI; "Claude Code" and "Codex" are their trademarks.

Roadmap

  • What needs you, the second layer: a step above the cards that decides for you what is plainly the agent's to do, and turns a long reply into steps
  • Cards for sessions running in a terminal or an editor, not only those Taskcue runs
  • More agents through the Agent Client Protocol: Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Goose and others
  • Continue a conversation in another agent, with a hand-off summary
  • Arrange cards freely and keep the layout
  • Sessions that keep running when the server restarts
  • A desktop app

Contributing

Issues and ideas are very welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request.

License

AGPL-3.0. You can use, change and share Taskcue freely; if you run a changed version as a service for others, you share your changes under the same license.

  • One board for every agent. Each project folder is a frame; each session is a card with its agent, its state (working, needs you, ready, stopped) and what it was asked.
  • Claude Code and Codex, side by side. Start either in any project, pick its model, and choose how much it may do without asking.
  • Approvals in one place. When an agent wants to run a command or edit a file, the card turns amber and the panel shows exactly what it wants to do: Allow, Allow for this session, or Deny.
  • Your existing sessions too. Recent conversations from Claude Code's and Codex's own history appear on the board. Open one to read it; send a message to continue it.
  • 仅限本地。 The server listens on 127.0.0.1 and checks a secret token on every call, so other websites and programs on your computer can't drive your agents.

What needs you

The page Taskcue opens on. At the top, every session Taskcue runs that is waiting on you, across agents and projects: agents asking before they act, and cards for turns that ended on something for you. Below them, what is working and what is ready, each with its last reply in a line.

A card holds what the reply asks, in plain words:

  • Its options, each with what the reply says it costs and gets you, and the one it recommends marked. Picked options turn green; a question you could want several answers to takes several picks.
  • One main button, named for what it sends: Send “MIT”, Send 2 answers, Send “Done” for a step you did, Send it back when the agent could have done it itself. Hover it to read the exact message. With nothing picked it sends the recommended answer; with only your own words typed, it sends your words.
  • Decline tells the session no and is final: that ask doesn't come back from that session, however it's worded.
  • The X takes a card off with nothing sent, and is final too.
  • The files the turn wrote, one press away.

When you write to a session yourself, its card steps aside until the session replies; the reading of that reply takes its place. A card you decided never comes back.

What it costs. Each finished turn is read once, by one short call on the agent you already use, with no tools and nothing saved to its history: Sonnet on Claude Code (about 3 seconds), or Codex's own model at low effort. It runs on your own sign-in and counts toward your plan like any other use. TASKCUE_READER=0 turns it off.

Tuning it. pnpm replay reads your own recent Claude Code turns the same way and writes a report of the cards it would have made to ~/.taskcue/replay/ (never commit it: it holds your conversations). To try other instructions, put them in ~/.taskcue/reader.md. More in docs/needs-you.md.

要求

  • Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm
  • At least one agent, installed and signed in: Claude Code: install it, then run claude once to sign in. Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex, then codex login. (On macOS, the copy inside the ChatGPT desktop app is found too.)
  • macOS or Linux. Windows is untested.

快速启动

git clone https://github.com/taskcue/taskcue.git
cd taskcue

Open the address it prints; it ends in #token=…. 就是这样。

设置

多变的 默认 它的作用
TASKCUE_PORT 4880 The port the server listens on (always 127.0.0.1).
TASKCUE_DATA_DIR ~/.taskcue Taskcue's own state: settings, the session list, the cards, the token.
TASKCUE_HISTORY on 0 keeps sessions from the agents' own history off the board.
TASKCUE_CLAUDE_BIN 在路径上找到 The claude binary to use.
TASKCUE_CODEX_BIN 在路径上找到 The codex binary to use.
TASKCUE_READER the session's own agent Which agent reads finished turns: claude, codex, or 0 for none (no cards).
TASKCUE_READER_MODEL Sonnet; Codex's default The model the reader asks for, by its agent's name for it. Set it with TASKCUE_READER.

权限

Each session starts in one of three modes, mapped onto each agent's own settings:

Mode 克劳德·科德 Codex
Ask first (default) default permission mode untrusted approvals, workspace-write sandbox
Edit freely acceptEdits on-request approvals, workspace-write sandbox
Full access bypassPermissions no approvals, no sandbox

Full access means the agent can run anything without asking. Use it only in a folder you'd trust it with.

它是如何运作的

browser (React, React Flow)  ──HTTP + SSE──▶  server (Node, no framework)
                                                │
                                                ├─ adapters/claude ──stdio, stream-json──▶  claude -p …
                                                └─ adapters/codex  ──stdio, JSON-RPC────▶  codex app-server

Each agent sits behind one small interface (server/agents/types.ts): start or resume a session, send a message, interrupt, answer an approval, read history. An adapter translates its agent's own events into Taskcue's (messages, tool calls, approvals) and the rest of the app never sees an agent's wire format. Conversations stay where each agent keeps them (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions); Taskcue only remembers which sessions are on the board.

More in docs/architecture.md. Adding another agent (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, anything that speaks the Agent Client Protocol) is one adapter: docs/adding-an-agent.md.

Your accounts

Taskcue runs each agent's own, unmodified program, and you sign in to it the agent's own way. Taskcue never reads, stores or forwards your credentials, and your usage is billed to your own account under your agreement with that provider. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI; "Claude Code" and "Codex" are their trademarks.
